sensors.name: left light sensor LLIGHT (light from above)

control_flow: driveInTheDark: if the left light sensor reads less than 30 %, drive forward forever; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Drive into a tunnel and come out at the other end.

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads less than 30 %

branches.reason: A tunnel is the only dark place the simulator has, and even deep inside it the light is 40 %, so the left light sensor is never below 30 %.
branches.outcome: light below 30 %: it drives forward on and on
light 30 % or more: it goes on to check for a wall
an obstacle is ahead: it stops
nothing ahead: it follows the line

input_dimensions.dimension: what is ahead of the robot in the tunnel
where the robot starts relative to the line
what is ahead of the robot

equivalence_classes: a wall in front of it
input_dimensions.dimension: what is ahead of the robot

scenarios.coded_response: The light reads 40 %, not below 30 %, so it checks the obstacle sensor; nothing is ahead, so it follows the line; the tunnel's plain floor is no black, so it curves right and circles into the tunnel wall.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot stands in a straight tunnel, in dim light, with nothing in front of it and no line on the floor.
scenarios.trigger: The program starts and the robot drives on.
scenarios.title: Drives through the tunnel without a line
assumptions: You didn't say there is a line in the tunnel: the program's dark branch drives straight on without one.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It drives straight through the tunnel and comes out at the other end.

scenarios.coded_response: The light is 40 % or more, so it checks the obstacle sensor; nothing is ahead, so it follows the line, curving left on black and right on the floor.
scenarios.initial_condition: A line runs through a tunnel, and the robot starts on it or beside it, with nothing ahead.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then the floor, again and again.
scenarios.title: Follows the line through the tunnel
assumptions: You didn't say there is a line through the tunnel.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line through the tunnel and comes out at the other end.

scenarios.coded_response: The light is 30 % or more, so it checks the obstacle sensor; it sees the wall and stops.
scenarios.initial_condition: A wall stands in front of the robot, in bright light.
scenarios.trigger: The obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall ahead
assumptions: You didn't say it, but the program is built to stop at a wall.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops in front of the wall without bumping into it.

uncertainties: A tunnel never gets darker than 40 %, so the left light sensor is never below 30 % and the branch that drives forward in the dark never happens.
You didn't say whether there is a line through the tunnel, and the program only gets through one by following a line.

tests.name: Gets through the tunnel to the goal
tests.scenario: Given the robot stands on the line inside a tunnel, in dim light, with nothing in front of it, when the program runs, then it follows the line through the tunnel and comes out at the other end, into Goal 1.

equivalence_partitions.selected_realization: a straight tunnel t2 with nothing inside it, the robot in its middle, 10 cm inside the opening
equivalence_partitions.dimension: what is ahead of the robot in the tunnel

expected_results: The robot drives through the tunnel along the line and comes out at the other end, into Goal 1.

postconditions.description: By the end of the run, the robot has come out of the tunnel and touched Goal 1.
During the whole run, it never bumps into the tunnel's walls.

assumptions: You said to get through the tunnel; the line through it is only there because your program needs one to drive on.

tests.reason: You said the robot should get through the tunnel; this test checks that it comes out the other side.

tests.name: On the line, it follows it through the tunnel
tests.scenario: Given a line running through a tunnel, when the program runs from a start on the line, then it follows the line through the tunnel and comes out at the other end into Goal 1, without bumping into the tunnel.

equivalence_partitions.selected_realization: A stands on the line's first point, facing along it

equivalence_partitions.selected_realization: nothing stands in the tunnel or on the line: the tunnel's walls run along the robot and the line goes through it
equivalence_partitions.dimension: what is ahead of the robot

expected_results: It follows the line into the tunnel, through it, and comes out at the other end into Goal 1.

postconditions.description: By the end of the run, the robot has touched Goal 1 outside the tunnel's exit.
During the whole run, it never bumps into the tunnel.

assumptions: You didn't say there is a line through the tunnel: the test gives it one, because your program only gets through by following a line.

tests.reason: Getting through the tunnel is what you asked for, and this is the typical start on the line.
